protocol: D-000 new cycle, turn 1 of 3; refute not confirm; RULE-GOVERNED SATISFIED re-record of DR-102 under adopted D-056 Class A plus a D-001 MF-6 file-08 edit
reviewGrade: This review is offered as the dedicated SATISFIED-GRADE review that D-056 Eligibility gate 4 requires for DR-102. See gatesCertified.
summary: I read D-056's five gates from the adopted COORD text rather than from the entry's recitation, and checked each against DR-102's live state and against the contract artifact itself. Gates 1, 3 and 5 verify completely: T2-02 is genuinely D-001's standing Route-A acceptance property, D-015 records ACCEPT at 0 blockers with a reservation sweep returning zero acceptance reservations, DR-G21 sits in file 08 with the exact owner claimed, and all four replacement strings are verbatim and unique. The condition-2 arithmetic verifies against my own count of the thirty rows. Gate 2 holds on the merits — I traced all eight ID-DEPs to the rows they ride and confirmed the live bar names execution as the sole SATISFIED-bar — but the entry's demonstration of it is incomplete. The live cell names four categories of leftover and the recitation disposes of three, never mentioning the tensions; 'T-1', 'T-4' and 'tension' occur zero times in the subject. Since this review is the gate-4 review and gate 2 is the gate that could be wrong, the record has to show the enumeration was exhaustive.

gatesCertified.gate1_classA_T2-02_contract: CERTIFIED. Verified independently of the entry's recitation.
gatesCertified.gate2_remainder_is_only_execution: CERTIFIED ON THE MERITS, but the entry's recitation of it is incomplete — see D085-SF-1. I certify that DR-102's sole remaining acceptance-evidence member is execution of CC-1..CC-11 at DR-G21; I do not certify the entry's enumeration as complete.
gatesCertified.gate5_MF-6_records_SATISFIED_and_removes: CERTIFIED as specified; the replacement strings are verbatim and the bar is displaced rather than left standing.

objections.location: Subject, 'Eligibility recitation' item 2 ('Remainder is only execution'), and consequentially the replacement SATISFIED-bar text in Decision clause 4
objections.claim: The gate-2 demonstration omits one of the four leftover categories the live DR-102 cell names. The tensions T-1..T-4 are never mentioned, so the recitation does not show that the remainder is only execution — it shows that three of four leftover categories are not execution-blocking.
objections.why: D-056 gate 2 requires that the remainder be only execution or measurement, and the eligibility recitation is the entry's record that the gate was checked. The live cell enumerates four leftovers, each introduced as a distinct category: execution of the conformance classes routed to DR-G21 via ID-DEP-3; 'Advisories A-CPC2-01 and A-CPC2-02 → the first successor edit of this artifact'; 'Tensions T-1..T-4 remain REPORTED to their owners'; and 'Identity dependencies ID-DEP-1..8 remain open at their owners'. Recitation item 2 disposes of the first, the second and the fourth, and says nothing about the third. I confirmed the omission mechanically rather than by impression: the strings 'T-1', 'T-2', 'T-3', 'T-4', 'Tension' and 'tension' each occur zero times in the subject. The gap matters most at T-1. The contract's own tensionsObserved discipline is 'Reported, not resolved — per the authoring task … none is settled by this artifact', and T-1's pendingResolution ends 'Whether that split is the intended reading of file 02 is for the coordinator/reviewer to decide.' The register routes T-1 to DR-125 with the applied TypeScript contract's in-band Cancel controlling. Those are two different dispositions of the same tension, and neither of them is execution. A reader auditing gate 2 has to notice the tensions unaided, find that T-2/T-3 ride DR-107/DR-111, T-4 rides DR-103/DR-120 and T-1 rides DR-125 or a coordinator reading, and only then conclude that none is DR-102's own remainder. That reasoning is exactly what the recitation exists to record. Two further considerations raise this above pedantry. First, this review is the gate-4 SATISFIED-GRADE review, so the recitation plus this verdict are the permanent evidence that gate 2 was tested; certifying gate 2 against a list that silently drops a category leaves the record weaker than the check I actually performed. Second, D-056 names four rows eligible in kind — DR-102, DR-115, DR-119 and DR-123 — and this is the first performance, so the recitation's shape is the template the remaining three will follow.
objections.whyNotMustFix: The substance holds and nothing is silently closed. I verified that the tensions sentence sits outside both replacement targets, so it survives the MF-6 edit and stays visible in the cell; and the live bar sentence, which is the register's own statement of what keeps the row unSATISFIED, names exactly one thing — execution of the hostile-conformance classes at DR-G21 via ID-DEP-3. The defect is in the completeness of the demonstration, not in the conclusion.
objections.repair: Extend recitation item 2 with a clause disposing of the tensions on the same terms as the other categories — that T-1..T-4 are REPORTED to owners on other rows (DR-125; DR-107/DR-111; DR-103/DR-120), are not acceptance-evidence members of DR-102, and were not reservations at D-015 — and say where T-1's 'for the coordinator/reviewer to decide' clause stands after D-015's 0-blocker acceptance. Mirroring one clause in the replacement bar text, which currently preserves only execution and the advisories, would make the cell self-describing on all four.

notesNonBlocking.location: Subject, Decision clause 4, the two DR-102 cell replacements
notesNonBlocking.observation: The two replacement targets treat markdown bold inconsistently. The lead target is quoted with its own '**' delimiters included and replaced by text that carries none, while the SATISFIED-bar target is quoted without them — I checked the bytes on either side of the match and found '. **' before and '** |' after, so the emphasis markers lie outside the quoted string. Replacing only the inner text therefore leaves the existing '**' pair wrapping the new five-sentence block, rendering all of it bold, where today it wraps a single sentence. Nothing false results and the cell stays well-formed, but the two edits in the same clause should state their treatment of the delimiters the same way.

whatIVerified: Subject digest at start and end: dedb17b5fc7acf5a5167ce9026b4f7157347e0be2dfea9a17971d8191d446874, three measurements each, equal to the dispatched value, -r--r--r-- at both ends. Prompt held at 60c2c631… across start and end.

I took D-056's five Eligibility gates from the adopted COORD text, not from this entry's recitation of them, so that the gates I tested against were not the ones the subject chose to state: Class A T2-02 contract or Class B DECIDED-V1-NOT-INTEGRATED; remainder is only execution or measurement; remainder already named at a condition-4 / DR-G* obligation with an owner; dedicated later SATISFIED-GRADE review; and an MF-6 that records SATISFIED and removes the cell-level execution or measurement bar. D-056 also names DR-102 among the four rows 'eligible in kind, not performed'.

Gate 1 verifies, including the citation I most suspected. 'T2-02' is not a loose label: D-001 records the 'Standing route-A acceptance property (T2-02) … a candidate is applicable when its independent review returns 0 blockers AND grants application-grade acceptance with no express reservation', so D-056's 'Class A T2-02 contract' and D-015's 'Route-A acceptance property: MET' are the same property under two names. D-015 records the subject at c50a79fe… and the verdict at 93762669…, both matching live bytes, as 'ACCEPT, 0 blockers, 2 new advisories (A-CPC2-01/02)', with a reservation-language sweep of the verdict returning 'zero acceptance reservations' and 'No apply-conditions'. The lead label is OPEN, as the recitation states.

The rejected alternative about the advisories therefore holds on evidence rather than assertion: D-015 classifies A-CPC2-01 and A-CPC2-02 as advisories arising with a 0-blocker acceptance and explicitly finds zero acceptance reservations, so treating them as eligibility-blocking design leftovers would contradict the adopted record.

Gate 2 holds on the merits, which I established from the contract artifact rather than from the register's summary of it. All eight identity dependencies name the surface they ride: ID-DEP-1 rides DR-103, ID-DEP-2 DR-007's successor chain, ID-DEP-4 DR-112/DR-G07/DR-107, ID-DEP-5 DR-125/DR-105, ID-DEP-6 DR-107, ID-DEP-8 DR-111, and ID-DEP-7 rides nothing by construction — it exists precisely to record that this contract does not ride the canonical encoding profile. Only ID-DEP-3 rides DR-G21, and its consequence text is the one that governs this row: 'DR-102's acceptance-evidence cell is discharged only when a harness executes them.' So the entry's claim that other ID-DEPs ride other rows is true of all seven, and the single remaining acceptance-evidence member is execution.

The strongest evidence for gate 2 is the register's own bar. The live sentence reads that the row 'remains slice-affecting and open until the hostile-conformance classes are executed by a harness at DR-G21 via ID-DEP-3' — one condition, and it is execution. D-015 says the same from the other side: 'the row stays OPEN, because the classes are specifications and no harness executes them.'

Gate 3 verifies against file 08 directly: DR-G21 COMPONENT-FAILURE-CONTAINMENT exists as a row with owner 'Supervisor + protocol + operability', character for character as the recitation claims, at assurance stage 'PROPOSED; not QUALIFIED' and status OPEN.

Gate 5's mechanics verify. All four replacement targets are present in file 08 verbatim and exactly once: the DR-102 lead, the SATISFIED-bar sentence, the condition-2 'Measured now' cell, and the clause 'condition 2 remains 0 of 30 SATISFIED'. A replacement aimed at a string that occurs once cannot hit the wrong cell.

The condition-2 arithmetic verifies against my own count rather than the entry's. I parsed the thirty DR-1xx rows and tallied their lead labels: 23 OPEN, 5 DECIDED-V1-NOT-INTEGRATED, 2 PROPOSED-CLOSED-FOR-REVIEW, zero SATISFIED, summing to 30, with DR-102's own lead reading OPEN. Moving DR-102 from OPEN to SATISFIED gives exactly the entry's 1 SATISFIED and 22 OPEN, and 1 + 22 + 5 + 2 is 30.

The new condition-2 cell also correctly dissolves the joint sentence. Today DR-102 and DR-103 are described together as carrying accepted design contracts and remaining OPEN; the replacement separates them, keeping DR-103 OPEN on its fixture-corpus authoring half. That matches D-056's 'D-013's SATISFIED-refusal stands until fixture authoring exists.'

The attack 'stale What that means 0 of 30' fails, and I checked the rest of the paragraph rather than only the clause the entry names. Its other count — 'condition 1 is met by one SATISFIED row plus ten scoped preview dispositions' — concerns the DR-001–011 set, which contains no DR-1xx row, so a DR-102 flip does not touch it. The paragraph's condition-4 and condition-5 statements are likewise unaffected.

I swept file 08 for every other mention of DR-102 in case a claim elsewhere goes stale. There are three: its own row, the condition-2 cell being rewritten, and DR-203's 'Source pin / affected sections' column, which lists 'DR-102/107/118/125/127' as a cross-reference and asserts nothing about DR-102's status. Nothing else needs an edit.

I also tested the DR-102 row's own Blueprint impact column, which the entry does not edit. It reads 'Hard blocker for component protocol blueprint — design contract ACCEPTED (D-015); the hostile-conformance execution half remains, at DR-G21', and it stays true after the flip: architecture SATISFIED under D-056 does not discharge execution, condition 5 remains gated on conditions 1, 2 and 4, and the column already names the execution half as the reason. Leaving it unchanged is correct rather than an oversight.

The attack 'this entry itself marks SATISFIED or applies file 08 before adoption' fails. Status is DRAFT, recitation item 5 conditions the write on adoption — 'This cycle's MF-6 edit, on adoption, records SATISFIED' — and file 08 measures ff2ebadd… unchanged, matching the pin and unmodified in my working tree.

The attack 'applies the split to DR-103' fails on three surfaces: clause 5's 'Does not mark DR-103, DR-115, DR-119, or DR-123 SATISFIED', the rejected alternative naming D-056's ineligible table, and the replacement condition-2 cell keeping DR-103 OPEN.

The attack 'leaves the until-executed bar live after the claimed SATISFIED' fails: clause 4 replaces that exact sentence, and the alternative 'Mark SATISFIED without removing the until executed bar. Rejected: D-056 Eligibility (5); two live SATISFIED rules' shows the entry understands why the displacement is mandatory rather than tidy.

The attack 'treats execution as architecture SATISFIED' fails. Clause 2 states that CC-1..CC-11 execution 'remains owed at DR-G21 as condition 4 / DR-012 qualification. It is not architecture SATISFIED evidence', which is D-056's split stated in D-056's own terms, and the replacement bar repeats it in the cell.

The attacks 'claims QUALIFIED / DEMONSTRATED' and 'authorizes docs/v2/implementation/' both fail: every occurrence in the subject is a refusal, the readiness effect records 'Zero QUALIFIED' and 'Condition 5 remains NOT MET and last', and the rejected alternative on implementation survives.

All seven measured inputs match live bytes: COORD 6dd90409…, file 08 ff2ebadd…, freeze e809d439…, the contract c50a79fe… and its verdict 93762669…, and both commits resolve at full hash — 75c981dd… to D-056 and 14865abc… to 'D-086: record gate-harness-naming.v3 as C4 candidate'. D-085 is absent from COORD, so adoption creates no collision.
COORD and file 08 are unmodified in my working tree. I wrote one file, the verdict named for me, and edited and committed nothing.
whatIDidNotCheck: The Codex review of this entry. Not read; no such file exists at review time.

control-protocol-contract.v2.review-independent.json itself. I hashed it at 937626695418d1cad10962bdded0d2aa29dadb005b345408edb7e8fbdc84b015, matching the pin, but did not open it, because it is another reviewer's verdict file and the standing instruction not to read those is one I would rather over-apply than under-apply. This is a real limit: my finding that A-CPC2-01 and A-CPC2-02 are advisories rather than acceptance reservations rests on D-015's adopted record of that verdict and on the live DR-102 cell, two independent secondary sources, not on the verdict's own text. If the coordinator wants that claim certified from the primary source, it needs a reviewer who has not been told to avoid it.

Whether the four tensions are correctly routed on their merits — that is, whether DR-125, DR-107, DR-111, DR-103 and DR-120 are the right owners for T-1..T-4. I verified that the cell and the contract route them off this row, which is what gate 2 turns on, not that the destinations are apt.

Whether CC-1..CC-11 are adequate hostile-conformance classes, and whether the contract's design is sound. D-015 accepted the contract at 0 blockers; this review takes that acceptance as the recorded fact gate 1 refers to and does not re-open it.
The merits of D-056 itself. I reviewed both its turns and consented at turn 2; this entry performs D-056 rather than amending it, and I did not re-audit the amendment.
Whether the file-08 write, once performed, will match this specification. This review is of the instruction; the resulting bytes are a later act under the C-D085 commit.

objectionNote: I OBJECT with zero MUST-FIX and one SHOULD-FIX. This is the first SATISFIED any V2 row has been given, so I tested the gates against D-056's adopted text rather than against the entry's account of them, and I checked the one citation that could have been a family confusion — T2-02 turns out to be exactly what it claims, D-001's standing Route-A acceptance property, and D-015 meets it with a recorded reservation sweep. Gate 2 is the gate that could be wrong, and on the merits it is not: I traced every identity dependency to the row it rides, and only ID-DEP-3 rides this one. But the entry's recitation of gate 2 walks past a whole category. The live cell lists four leftovers and the recitation answers three; the tensions are not mentioned once, and T-1 is the one whose disposition the contract expressly leaves to the coordinator or reviewer. Because my verdict is the gate-4 review, what I certify has to rest on an enumeration that is visibly complete, and because three more rows are eligible in kind, this recitation is the form the next three will copy. Adding the missing clause costs a sentence.
